---
title: "North Carolina"
subtitle: "November 2026 results"
---

```{r}
#| label: setup
#| include: false

library(tidyverse)
library(sf)
library(leaflet)
library(plotly)
library(tigris)

read_nc_results <- \(path) {
  read_tsv(path, show_col_types = FALSE)
}

county_margins <- \(results, contest, candidates) {
  results |>
    filter(`Contest Name` == contest,
           Choice %in% names(candidates)) |>
    mutate(party = recode(Choice, !!!candidates)) |>
    group_by(County, party) |>
    summarize(votes = sum(`Total Votes`), .groups = "drop") |>
    pivot_wider(names_from = party, values_from = votes, values_fill = 0) |>
    mutate(margin = 100 * (DEM - REP) / (DEM + REP),
           county_name = str_to_title(County))
}

results_2026 <- read_nc_results(
  "data/north-carolina/2026-11-03/results_pct_20261103.txt"
)
results_2024 <- read_nc_results(
  "data/north-carolina/2024-11-05/results_pct_20241105.txt"
)

senate_2026 <- county_margins(
  results_2026,
  "US SENATE",
  c("Roy Cooper" = "DEM", "Michael Whatley" = "REP")
) |>
  select(county_name, margin_2026 = margin,
         dem_2026 = DEM, rep_2026 = REP)

president_2024 <- county_margins(
  results_2024,
  "US PRESIDENT",
  c("Kamala D. Harris" = "DEM", "Donald J. Trump" = "REP")
) |>
  select(county_name, margin_2024 = margin,
         dem_2024 = DEM, rep_2024 = REP)

county_comparison <- senate_2026 |>
  inner_join(president_2024, by = "county_name") |>
  mutate(swing = margin_2026 - margin_2024)

counties <- counties(state = "NC", year = 2024, cb = TRUE) |>
  mutate(county_name = str_to_title(NAME)) |>
  st_transform(4326)

county_map <- counties |>
  left_join(county_comparison, by = "county_name")

county_totals_2026 <- senate_2026 |>
  summarize(dem = sum(dem_2026), rep = sum(rep_2026)) |>
  mutate(margin = 100 * (dem - rep) / (dem + rep),
         margin_text = paste0(if_else(margin > 0, "D+", "R+"),
                              abs(round(margin, 1))))
```

## 2026 U.S. Senate

The map shows the Democratic margin in percentage points by county:
**D+** means Roy Cooper led Michael Whatley in that county.

```{r}
#| label: senate-map
#| fig-width: 9

pal <- colorBin(
  palette = c("#b2182b", "#ef8a62", "#f7f7f7", "#67a9cf", "#2166ac"),
  bins = c(-100, -20, -5, 5, 20, 100),
  domain = county_map$margin_2026,
  na.color = "#bdbdbd"
)

leaflet(county_map, options = leafletOptions(zoomSnap = 0.25)) |>
  addProviderTiles(providers$CartoDB.Positron) |>
  addPolygons(
    fillColor = ~pal(margin_2026),
    fillOpacity = 0.82,
    color = "white",
    weight = 0.7,
    label = ~paste0(
      county_name, ": ",
      if_else(margin_2026 > 0, "D+", "R+"),
      abs(round(margin_2026, 1))
    ),
    highlightOptions = highlightOptions(
      weight = 2,
      color = "#333333",
      fillOpacity = 0.95,
      bringToFront = TRUE
    )
  ) |>
  addLegend(
    position = "bottomright",
    pal = pal,
    values = ~margin_2026,
    title = "Democratic margin",
    labFormat = labelFormat(suffix = "%")
  )
```

## County shift from 2024

The chart compares each county's 2026 Senate margin with its 2024 presidential
margin. Positive values mean a more Democratic result in 2026 relative to 2024.

```{r}
#| label: swing-chart
#| fig-width: 9
#| fig-height: 7

plot <- ggplot(county_comparison,
               aes(x = margin_2024, y = margin_2026,
                   text = county_name,
                   color = swing)) +
  geom_abline(intercept = 0, slope = 1, linetype = "dashed",
              color = "gray50") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linewidth = 0.3, color = "gray70") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linewidth = 0.3, color = "gray70") +
  geom_point(size = 2.5, alpha = 0.85) +
  scale_color_gradient2(
    low = "#b2182b", mid = "#f7f7f7", high = "#2166ac",
    midpoint = 0
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "2026 Senate margin vs. 2024 presidential margin",
    x = "2024 Harris margin (percentage points)",
    y = "2026 Cooper margin (percentage points)",
    color = "Swing toward Democrats"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 13)

ggplotly(plot, tooltip = "text")
```

## Data coverage

- **2026 source:** NCSBE precinct results, November 3, 2026
- **2024 source:** NCSBE precinct results, November 5, 2024
- **2026 geographic scale:** precinct results aggregated to counties
- **Future geographic scale:** Census or NCSBE precinct boundaries
- **Candidates shown:** Roy Cooper vs. Michael Whatley, and
  Kamala Harris vs. Donald Trump

The underlying 2026 and 2024 files are stored in
`data/north-carolina/2026-11-03/` and
`data/north-carolina/2024-11-05/`.
